what_its_for: Moexipril is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering your blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It belongs to a group of medicines called ACE inhibitors, which work by relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Take moexipril by mouth, usually once or twice a day. It is very important to take this medicine on an EMPTY STOMACH, at least 1 hour before a meal. Food can reduce how well the medicine works. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 7.5 mg once daily, taken 1 hour before a meal. Your doctor may increase your dose over time, up to a maximum of 30 mg per day (taken as one dose or split into two doses). Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but ONLY if it is still several hours before your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store moexipril at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor approves, because moexipril can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can further lower your blood pressure and cause dizziness or fainting. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine may cause dizziness, especially when you first start taking it. Avoid taking anti-inflammatory pain relievers (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without checking with your doctor, as they can reduce the effectiveness of moexipril and may harm your kidneys. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant — it can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this is called angioedema and is a serious allergic reaction); difficulty breathing or swallowing; a severe skin rash; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness and tingling; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination; fainting or severe dizziness; persistent dry cough that is bothersome (a common side effect — your doctor may switch you to a different medicine); yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to notice a small decrease in blood pressure within 1 to 2 hours after your first dose, with the greatest effect occurring within 3 to 6 hours. However, it may take several weeks of regular use to get the full benefit of this medicine. Even if you feel well, keep taking it — high blood pressure often has no symptoms. Do not stop taking moexipril without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Do NOT use moexipril during pregnancy. It can cause serious injury or death to your unborn baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: It is not known if moexipril passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. KIDNEY DISEASE: Your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor your kidney function and potassium levels more closely. ELDERLY PATIENTS: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and dizziness of this medicine. Use caution when standing up. CHILDREN: Moexipril has not been studied in children and is not recommended for use in patients under 18 years of age.
